say: The hackathon brief asked for an agent that does one specific job. | So I built mine for the live map: | it watches every car on the road. | When a car stands still for twenty-six minutes, and the plan doesn't say why, | a plain rule spots the stop, | then the agent does the cheap work first. | It checks the G P S is fresh, | then the places lookup finds a fuel station, a cafe and a truck park, | and a decision model ranks why the car stopped. | It reads the driver's chat and works out the arrival time. | Fuel stop, safe arrival: it logs it and stays quiet. | Odd place or stale signal: it asks the driver first. | A breakdown or a late delivery: | one person gets one decision.
show: The hackathon brief asked for an agent that does one specific job. | So I built mine for the live map: | it watches every car on the road. | When a car stands still for 26 minutes, and the plan doesn't say why, | a plain rule spots the stop, | then the agent does the cheap work first. | It checks the GPS is fresh, | then the places lookup finds a fuel station, a café and a truck park, | and a decision model ranks why the car stopped. | It reads the driver's chat and works out the arrival time. | Fuel stop, safe arrival: it logs it and stays quiet. | Odd place or stale signal: it asks the driver first. | A breakdown or a late delivery: | one person gets one decision.

say: Those checks run on Baan-ator one point one, pro preview, my fine-tuned model. | It is Liquid A I's d1, a three billion parameter model that reads text and images, | with a LoRA adapter I trained on top. | I also fine-tuned Laya, a four hundred twenty-one million parameter decision model from ConvAI. | Seven training runs in all: six for Laya, one for d1. | My case generator made fifteen thousand unique cases from six hundred seventy-six template families. | I locked two hundred and three families away: four thousand three hundred ninety-five cases the models never saw. | The models trained on the rest. | On those unseen cases, Baan-ator is right ninety-three point five percent of the time. | Jev, the commercial checker, is right eighty-nine point three percent. | Laya, fine-tuned: eighty-eight. | The base models, as released: sixty-five percent and lower. | Fine-tuning cut false alarms from thirty-three percent to five. | Jev raises thirteen. | Baan-ator answers in twenty-two milliseconds. | Jev takes two hundred twenty-nine, | and costs about three times as much per check. | The winning run took twenty-four minutes on one NVIDIA G P U at Verda, in Finland, | for one dollar thirty-three.
show: Those checks run on bahnator-1.1-pro-preview, my fine-tuned model. | It is Liquid AI's d1, a 3-billion-parameter model that reads text and images, | with a LoRA adapter I trained on top. | I also fine-tuned Laya, a 421-million-parameter decision model from ConvAI. | Seven training runs in all: six for Laya, one for d1. | My case generator made 15,000 unique cases from 676 template families. | I locked 203 families away: 4,395 cases the models never saw. | The models trained on the rest. | On those unseen cases, bahnator is right 93.5% of the time. | Jev, the commercial checker, is right 89.3%. | Laya, fine-tuned: 88%. | The base models, as released: 65% and lower. | Fine-tuning cut false alarms from 33% to 5%. | Jev raises 13%. | bahnator answers in 22 milliseconds. | Jev takes 229, | and costs about three times as much per check. | The winning run took 24 minutes on one NVIDIA GPU at Verda, in Finland, | for $1.33.
